svg.text: this deployment · one CloudFormation root stack
connected from the Agent Spaces screen
S3 origin · WAF on by default
How an administrator connects accounts, onboards databases, schedules collection and governs users, models and knowledge
invites · groups · roles · sign-out on role change
then verify with a real login
The administrator signs in with Amazon Cognito (TOTP) and loads the admin console from CloudFront. Super admins see everything; space admins see their
spaces, their capability tier and Monitoring.
Every action is a REST call through API Gateway (JWT authorizer) and the VPC Link to the FastAPI service on ECS Fargate; privileged changes are written
Agent Spaces, connected accounts, database records, network connections, governance (models, knowledge, invites) and the audit trail live in DynamoDB;
knowledge documents in S3; the model catalog is read from Bedrock.
Connecting an account: you create a read-only IAM role that trusts the agent with the space's ExternalId; the console assumes it to discover RDS and
Aurora databases, validate the read-only secret against the database's own endpoint, and set up VPC peering or PrivateLink, then verifies with a real
Monitoring: one Tier 1 and one Tier 2 schedule per physical database in EventBridge Scheduler (cadence, pause/resume, shared by every space that includes
the database); Collection shows each database's newest rows in the metrics store.
Settings (super admins): Users and Operators manage the Cognito pool with invites over Amazon SES; Email configures the sender; Alarms switches the
per-database email alarms on or off, all or each, and sends a test email; Security reads the live posture, the cost budget and the guardrail alarms, and
names this deployment's CloudFormation stack, where the optional controls are parameters.
Diagram uses the AWS Architecture Icons (aws.amazon.com/architecture/icons).
